Which 1907 film is counted as the first Finnish feature film?
Salaviinanpolttajat was directed by Teuvo Puro for Atelier Apollo in 1907.
Which Minna Canth play became a silent film of which only 13 minutes survive?
Teuvo Puro filmed Sylvi in 1911; it premiered in 1913 and survives only in fragments.
Who founded Suomi-Filmi and later walked out to found its rival studio?
Karu led Suomi-Filmi from 1919, was ousted in 1933 and founded Suomen Filmiteollisuus.
Which 1923 film is held to be the masterpiece of the Finnish silent era?
Erkki Karu's Nummisuutarit, from Aleksis Kivi's play, is the silent film most often named.
What was the first Finnish full-length film with both song and spoken dialogue, in 1931?
Lahyn-Filmi's Sano se suomeksi brought sound to the Finnish feature in 1931.
Which 1956 film was Finland's first feature-length colour film?
Toivo Särkkä's Juha, from Juhani Aho's novel, was the first Finnish feature in colour.
Which Finnish film producer and director made more than 200 feature films?
Särkkä led Suomen Filmiteollisuus until its bankruptcy in 1965 and is the most prolific of all.
In which 1962 film did the young Vesa-Matti Loiri make his screen debut?
Mikko Niskanen's Pojat, from Paavo Rintala's novel, launched both director and star.
Edvin Laine's 1968 film Here, Beneath the North Star tells the civil war from whose side?
Täällä Pohjantähden alla, from Väinö Linna's trilogy, follows the Red Guards.
The Jussi for Best Film was not given at all for five years. Which years?
Introduced in 1986, the award lapsed from 1987 to 1991 and returned in 1992.
Which war film won the Jussi for Best Film in 1999?
Olli Saarela's Rukajärven tie took the best film Jussi at the 54th gala.
Who has won the Jussi for Best Film more often than anyone else?
Kaurismäki has six wins; Pölönen, Kari Sara and Aleksi Bardy have four each.
Since 2008 the Jussi for Best Film has gone to whom?
Until 2008 it went to director, producer and company together; now to the producer alone.
In which town was the painter Albert Edelfelt born, and in which did he die?
Edelfelt was born at Porvoo in 1854 and died there in 1905; the town has his museum.
Which French scientist did Albert Edelfelt paint in his laboratory in 1885?
The Pasteur portrait was shown at the 1886 Paris Salon and made Edelfelt's European name.
Which honour did Edelfelt receive at the age of 35 after his Pasteur portrait?
The Order of the White Rose
France made him a member of the Legion of Honour on the strength of the portrait's success.
Which Edelfelt painting of 1884 was voted Finland's most significant painting in 2013?
Leikkiviä poikia rannalla came first in a 2013 poll of the nation's most important picture.
Whose poem cycle The Tales of Ensign Stål did Edelfelt illustrate in the 1890s?
Edelfelt's drawings for Vänrikki Stoolin tarinat became the standard images of the poems.
Edelfelt set up a studio in 1883 at a coastal manor near Porvoo. Which one?
His family bought the Haikko summer house in 1880; local people sat as his models.
Edelfelt's The Burnt Village of 1879 shows a scene from which Finnish uprising?
The picture of the 1596 peasant rising was praised at the Salon and ended his history painting.
Which years are usually given as the Golden Age of Finnish art?
The Golden Age runs roughly 1880-1910, the decades of the national awakening.
Which 1886 painting of two birds in combat is counted a seminal Finnish picture?
Ferdinand von Wright's Taistelevat metsot predates the Golden Age but shaped Finnish taste.
Which Eero Järnefelt painting of 1893 shows children at work clearing burnt-over land?
Raatajat rahanalaiset, also called Kaski, is Järnefelt's best-known social picture.
Which painter of the Golden Age is known for The Mower Men of 1891?
Halonen's Niittomiehet is among the best-known pictures of Finnish country labour.
Who sculpted Havis Amanda, the fountain statue of 1908 in Helsinki market square?
Vallgren's bronze maiden was unveiled in 1908 and is capped by students every May Day eve.
Which Finnish woman architect designed the Tampere central fire station of 1908?
Lönn was the first Finnish woman to run her own architect's office and built widely in Tampere.
Which painter laid the groundwork for Kalevala pictures long before Gallen-Kallela?
Ekman was the first notable painter of Kalevala subjects in Finnish art.
Which teacher is credited with training a whole generation of Golden Age Finnish painters?
Von Becker's private school and university teaching reached most of the era's artists.
Which Maria Wiik painting of 1889 shows a girl setting out from home?
Ulos maailmaan is the best-known work of Maria Wiik, one of the era's women painters.
Roughly how many people died in Finland's great hunger years of 1866 to 1868?
Some 270,000 died over the three years, about 8.5 per cent of the whole population.
Which Finnish statesman resisted borrowing abroad during the famine, fearing for the markka?
Snellman, in charge of finances, feared a high-interest loan would weaken the new currency.
From which bank did Finland finally borrow money in late 1867 to buy grain?
The State Bank in Saint Petersburg
The loan came too late: grain prices had already risen and the worst of the famine was on.
Which great public work was built as famine relief in Finland in the late 1860s?
Hungry men were set to dig the railway east, the largest relief work of the hunger years.
What stopped Finland's 1867 harvest and sealed the famine?
Night frosts in the first days of September 1867 cut the harvest to about half of normal.
In which year was the whole Bible first published in Finnish?
Agricola's New Testament came in 1548, but the complete Finnish Bible waited until 1642.
Which society, founded in 1831, organised the collecting of Finnish folk poetry?
Suomalaisen Kirjallisuuden Seura coordinated the collecting and published the folk poems.
How many volumes does Suomen kansan vanhat runot, the collected Finnish folk poems, fill?
The great edition of the old poems of the Finnish people fills 33 volumes.
Which Minna Canth play of 1885 started a quarrel about married women's rights?
In the play a drunken husband may keep his wife's money, because the law lets him.
Which Italian poet did Eino Leino translate into Finnish?
Leino, the great Finnish poet of his generation, put the Divine Comedy into Finnish.
Which 1919 novel was F. E. Sillanpää's book about the Finnish civil war?
Hurskas kurjuus follows a crofter who ends up shot as a Red in 1918.
Which 1905 novel by Johannes Linnankoski follows a logger and his many loves?
The book has been filmed again and again in Finland, for the first time in 1919.
In which Finnish town have the Tangomarkkinat been held every year since 1985?
The festival ends with the crowning of a tango king and queen.
Which instrument took the bandoneon's place when the tango became Finnish?
Finnish tango swapped the bandoneon for the accordion and added drums.
In which key is Finnish tango almost always written?
The minor key is so nearly universal in Finnish tango that a major one surprises.
In which year did the tango first reach Finland?
Travelling musicians brought it in 1913; Finns began writing their own tangos in the 1930s.
Which Finnish singer is remembered above all for Punatukkaiselle tytölleni?
Virta was the great voice of the Finnish tango's best years in the 1950s.
Which composer wrote the tango Liljankukka?
Kärki was the most prolific composer of Finnish popular song of his age.
Who wrote the first opera composed in Finland, staged in 1852?
Pacius's Kung Karls jakt came nearly fifty years before Sibelius's only opera.
Who founded the Helsinki Philharmonic Orchestra in 1883?
Kajanus's orchestra was among the first permanent ones in the Nordic countries.
Who founded in 1883 the music institute that grew into the Sibelius Academy?
Wegelius's Helsinki Music Institute is the ancestor of today's Sibelius Academy.
Which singer founded the Finnish Opera in 1911 and the first Savonlinna festival in 1912?
Ackté was the first Finnish soprano of international rank and an organiser besides.
Which Leevi Madetoja opera of 1924 is set among the people of Ostrobothnia?
Pohjalaisia became the best-loved Finnish opera before Sallinen's generation.
Which Finnish composer wrote string quartets in the 18th century, long before Sibelius?
Tulindberg is the earliest named Finnish composer of art music.
Which bowed Finnish folk instrument was brought back to life in the folk revival?
The jouhikko is a bowed lyre with horsehair strings, played again since the 1970s.
Which Finnish village has held a folk music festival every year since 1968?
Kaustinen was the home of the pelimanni revival and of Konsta Jylhä's band.
Which two well-known Finnish rock bands both came out of the town of Pori?
Pori produced two of the biggest Finnish bands of the 1980s at once.
Which Finnish band built a whole career on parodying humppa?
Eläkeläiset turn rock classics into humppa, the rural cousin of the iskelmä.
In which language does the Finnish rapper Amoc perform?
Amoc raps in Inari Sámi, a language with only a few hundred speakers.
Which Finnish folk group sings in the Kalevala metre with the kantele?
Värttinä took runo singing out of the archive and onto world stages.
In which city was Carl Ludvig Engel, the architect of Helsinki's Senate Square, born?
Engel was born in Charlottenburg in Berlin in 1778, into a family of master masons.
Before coming to Finland, Engel was town architect of which city?
He held the post in Tallinn from 1809 and moved on to Turku in 1814.
What was Helsinki City Hall, finished by Engel in 1833, originally built as?
Engel's building opened as a hotel before the city took it over for itself.
Which Finnish city did Engel replan after the great fire of 1827?
He drew fire-prevention plans for Turku and for several other Finnish towns.
Which man, rebuilding Helsinki, hired Engel to the reconstruction committee in 1816?
Ehrenström drew the new street plan and Engel filled it with buildings.
Who founded the company that became Nokia, in 1865?
Idestam, a mining engineer, put up a ground wood pulp mill on the Tammerkoski rapids.
On which rapids did Nokia's first mill stand?
The first mill was on Tammerkoski in Tampere; the second, from 1868, gave the firm its name.
In which year did the rubber works, cable works and paper mill merge into Nokia Corporation?
The three companies had long worked together before the formal merger of 1967.
How much did the Mobira Senator, Nokia's first car telephone of 1982, weigh?
The Senator weighed 9.8 kg and lived in the boot of the car, not in a pocket.
Which Soviet leader gave the Mobira Cityman its nickname Gorba?
Gorbachev was photographed using one in Helsinki in 1987 and the name stuck.
Who made the world's first GSM call, in Helsinki on 1 July 1991?
Holkeri spoke on a prototype Nokia handset over the first working GSM network.
What does the model number of the Nokia 1011, the first GSM phone, stand for?
The 1011 went on sale on 10 November 1992, and the date became its name.
To which company did Nokia sell its mobile phone business in 2014?
The sale went through in April 2014 for about 3.79 billion euros.
How many cases does Finnish usually count?
Fifteen are counted; the prolative survives only in frozen words such as postitse.
Which Finnish case does the ending -ksi mark, as in opettajaksi?
The translative marks a change of state: becoming something that one was not.
Which Finnish case means without, as in rahatta?
The abessive -tta is rare on its own but common with the third infinitive.
The Finnish word postitse is a fossil of which case?
The prolative, by way of, is no longer a living case and survives in set words only.
Which Finnish case is used with a possessive suffix to mean in company with?
The comitative, as in vaimoineen, is rare and almost unheard in speech.
The exessive case, meaning from being as, survives in which Finnish dialect?
Standard Finnish has no exessive; Savo dialects and Karelian still use the ending -nta.
Which Danish king reigned nearly sixty years, longer than any other?
Christian IV reigned from 1588 to 1648, founding towns and losing wars as he went.
In which year did the Danish crown become hereditary and absolute?
The change came under Frederik III, who had been elected on terms in 1648.
How many Danish kings have been called Christian?
Christian I to Christian X; the Frederiks number ten as well.
Which Danish king conquered England and ruled it from 1016?
Cnut held Denmark, England and Norway at once until his death in 1035.
Which queen ruled Denmark, Norway and Sweden from 1387 and built the Kalmar Union?
Margaret ruled as the real power until 1412 while a grand-nephew wore the crown.
Which Danish king is counted the first of the historical line, before Harald Bluetooth?
Gorm the Old, dead about 958, is the earliest Danish king the lists treat as historical.
In which centuries were the Sagas of Icelanders written down?
They were set down in the 13th and 14th centuries about events three hundred years older.
On what material were the Icelandic sagas chiefly written?
Vellum made from calfskin was the writing material of saga-age Iceland.
Which saga writer is thought by some scholars to have written Egil's Saga?
Snorri was a descendant of Egil's, which is one reason for the guess.
Which Icelandic saga tells of an outlaw poet and survives in two different versions?
Gísla saga Súrssonar follows an outlawed poet and comes down in two versions.
In which year did Norway declare that oil found off its coast belonged to Norway?
The claim came in May 1963, before anyone knew whether there was oil to claim.
What did a 1958 letter from the Geological Survey of Norway say about offshore oil?
That a vast field was certain
The experts advised that there was almost no chance of finding oil off the Norwegian coast.
On which day of the year was Norway's first great oil field found, in 1969?
The well that proved the big field came in on 24 December 1969.
In which year did Norway set up its oil fund, which saves petroleum money for later?
The fund began in 1990 and is part of the Government Pension Fund of Norway.
Which Swede invented the safety match?
Pasch moved the dangerous phosphorus out of the match head and onto the box.
Who invented the three-point seat belt, working at Volvo?
Volvo gave the patent away free so that every carmaker could use it.
Which Swede patented the adjustable spanner in 1892?
Johansson's pipe wrench and adjustable spanner are still in nearly every toolbox.
Who built the first small battery-powered pacemaker, in 1958?
Elmqvist, a Swedish engineer and doctor, made the first implantable pacemaker.
Which Swede invented the self-aligning ball bearing in 1907 and founded SKF?
Wingqvist's multi-row self-aligning radial ball bearing is from 1907.
Which Swedish invention of 1951 was the forerunner of the milk carton?
Erik Wallenberg's tetrahedral carton of 1951 became the Tetra Pak company.
Which Swede's milk-cream separator founded a company and changed dairy farming?
De Laval co-founded AB Separator in 1883 on the strength of his centrifuge.
Which Swedish doctor built one of the first practical dialysis machines?
Alwall's machine at Lund was among the first that could be used on patients.
What did the Finnish word löyly originally mean?
The word is old Finnic and its first sense was breath or spirit, not steam.
In which year was Finnish sauna culture added to the UNESCO intangible heritage list?
The inscription was made on 17 December 2020; Estonia's smoke saunas went on in 2014.
What makes a savusauna a smoke sauna?
The smoke fills the room while the wood burns, and the fire is out before anyone bathes.
The birch whisk is called vihta in which part of Finland?
It is vihta in western Finland and vasta in the east, and the border is old.
Besides bathing, what was the Finnish sauna traditionally used for?
The sauna served for births, laying out the dead, laundry, beer and curing meat.
What temperature is a Finnish sauna usually kept at?
The usual range is 80-90 °C, within a wider span of about 80-110 °C.
Which fell is the highest summit lying wholly inside Finland?
The top of Halti is on the Norwegian side, so Ridnitšohkka at 1,317 m is Finland's own highest.
In which Finnish region do all ten of the country's highest fells lie?
Every peak over 1,100 metres in Finland is in the Lapland arm in the far north-west.
Which 1899 decree began the first wave of Russification in Finland?
Nicholas II's manifesto of 15 February 1899 claimed imperial authority over Finnish law.
How many names were on the great petition that Finns took to the tsar in 1899?
A delegation of 500 carried the petition to Saint Petersburg, and the tsar refused to see them.
The Pro Finlandia petition of 1899 was signed by whom?
Writers, scientists and artists from abroad appealed to the tsar on Finland's behalf.
What did the Language Manifesto of 1900 make the language of Finnish administration?
A Russian minority of about 8,000 in 2.7 million was to run the Grand Duchy's offices.
What did Russia abolish in Finland in January 1901?
Finland's own stamps went, along with its army, its censorship-free press and much else.
What was the senate of 1909 to 1917 called, when officers replaced Finnish senators?
Finnish-born officers of the Russian army sat in place of civilian senators.
What were the sotilasmiljoonat, the military millions, that Russia demanded of Finland?
Payments in place of conscripting Finns
Finland paid cash instead of sending men into the Russian army.
Which ship carrying rifles for a Finnish uprising was wrecked off Finland in 1905?
Finnish activists had bought the guns with Japanese money during the Russo-Japanese War.
What did the Russian law of 1912 open to Russians in Finland?
All government and civil service posts
The Law of Equality let Russians take any Finnish office, however senior.
Which New York airport terminal, shaped like a bird in flight, did Eero Saarinen design?
Saarinen's TWA terminal at Idlewild was designed from 1956 and opened in 1962, after his death.
Which Washington airport's main terminal was designed by Eero Saarinen?
The Dulles terminal, with its hanging roof, was designed from 1958 and finished in 1963.
Which Eero Saarinen chair of the 1950s stands on a single stem instead of four legs?
The Tulip, part of his Pedestal series, was designed to clear the clutter of chair legs.
In which two European capitals did Eero Saarinen design United States embassy buildings?
Both chancelleries were designed in 1955 and finished at the end of that decade.
In which year did Eero Saarinen die, with several of his buildings still unfinished?
He died suddenly in 1961; the Gateway Arch and the TWA terminal were completed later.
How many sites make up the Aalto Works on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
Thirteen works by Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto were inscribed as one series.
Which city holds five of the thirteen Aalto World Heritage sites?
Helsinki has Finlandia Hall, the Aalto House, Studio Aalto, the House of Culture and KELA.
In which Finnish town does Alvar Aalto's Church of the Three Crosses stand?
The church at Vuoksenniska in Imatra is one of the thirteen World Heritage Aalto sites.
Alvar Aalto's Sunila pulp mill housing area, a World Heritage site, is in which town?
The workers' housing at Sunila in Kotka dates from the second half of the 1930s.
In which year was the Fiskars ironworks founded?
Queen Christina of Sweden granted a Dutch merchant a charter for a blast furnace in 1649.
In which year did Fiskars make its first pair of orange-handled scissors?
Prototypes came in black, red, green and orange, and the staff voted for orange.
How was the colour of the Fiskars scissor handle chosen?
By a vote among the staff
Four prototype colours were put to an internal vote, and orange won.
Which Danish porcelain house did Fiskars buy in 2013?
Fiskars had already bought Iittala in 2007 and added Royal Copenhagen six years later.
At which university was Linus Torvalds a student when he began the Linux kernel?
He announced his new operating system to a Usenet newsgroup on 25 August 1991.
Users of which operating system read Torvalds's first Linux announcement?
He posted to comp.os.minix that he was doing a free operating system, just a hobby.
On which Finnish server was the first Linux kernel put up in September 1991?
Version 0.01 went onto the Finnish university network's file server on 17 September 1991.
What is the name of the Linux mascot penguin?
Larry Ewing drew the penguin, and version 1.0 of the kernel came in March 1994.
Who was the first Finn to win the world rally drivers' title?
Alén took the 1978 title in a Fiat 131 Abarth.
Which Finn won the world rally title four years in a row from 1996?
Mäkinen won in 1996, 1997, 1998 and 1999, all in a Mitsubishi Lancer.
Which Finn won world rally titles with three different manufacturers?
Kankkunen won with Peugeot in 1986, Lancia in 1987 and 1991 and Toyota in 1993.
With which car did Hannu Mikkola win the 1983 world rally title?
Mikkola's title was the Quattro's first for a driver, a year before Blomqvist's.
Which Finn won the world rally title in 2022 and 2023?
Rovanperä took both titles in a Toyota GR Yaris Rally1.
Which was Lasse Virén's trade away from the running track?
He was a policeman from Myrskylä, and later sat in the Finnish parliament.
Where did Lasse Virén finish in the Olympic marathon of 1976, his first marathon ever?
He ran 2:13:11 for fifth place, days after winning the 5,000 and 10,000 metres.
What did Lasse Virén do after his running career?
He was a member of the Finnish parliament from 1999 to 2007 and again in 2010 and 2011.
Which flower is Finland's national flower?
Kielo, the lily of the valley, is the official national flower of Finland.
Which tree is Finland's national tree?
The birch is the national tree, though pine makes up far more of the forest.
Which fish is Finland's national fish?
The perch is the official national fish, the best known fish of the Finnish lakes.
Which stone is Finland's national stone?
Granite is the national stone, and the bedrock of most of the country.
Which insect is Finland's national insect?
The seven-spot ladybird, leppäkerttu, is the official national insect.
Which food is Finland's national food?
Dark rye bread is the official national food and a staple of the Finnish diet.
Which Finnish city is the home of mustamakkara, black sausage?
Mustamakkara is sold at the Tampere market hall and eaten with lingonberry jam.
Which Finnish pastry has been given EU protected geographical status?
The lingonberry pastry rönttönen carries a protected geographical indication.
On which day of the week is pea soup traditionally eaten in Finland?
Thursday pea soup is followed by pancakes, in canteens and in barracks alike.
On whose memorial day, 5 February, is the runebergintorttu eaten?
The little almond and arrack cake is named after the national poet.
What is vispipuuro, the pink Finnish pudding, made of?
Semolina porridge is whipped with lingonberry until it turns pale pink and light.
With what is Finnish leipäjuusto usually served?
The squeaky bread cheese is eaten warm with cloudberry jam beside the coffee cup.
Which Finnish dish is a cross between a crêpe and a flatbread, filled with farina?
Sultsina is made from unleavened rye dough and is sold around Joensuu in eastern Finland.
Which Sami language is spoken only inside Finland's borders?
Inari Sami has about 350 speakers and no community outside Finland.
How many Sami languages are counted in all?
Eleven are counted, of which three are spoken in Finland and several are extinct.
What does Sami National Day on 6 February commemorate?
The founding of the Sami parliament
The first Sami congress met at Trondheim in Norway on that day in 1917.
In which year was the Sami flag inaugurated?
The flag was raised at the Sami Conference in Åre in Sweden on 15 August 1986.
What do the two circles on the Sami flag stand for?
The red half-circle is the sun and the blue half-circle the moon.
Who may herd reindeer in Finland?
Anyone living in the herding area
In Norway and Sweden herding is reserved to the Sami; Finland leaves it open.
Where and when was the first game of pesäpallo played?
Lauri Pihkala's new game had its first match on 14 November 1920.
How is the ball delivered to the batter in pesäpallo?
Thrown straight up over the plate
The pitcher stands beside the plate and throws the ball at least a metre above his own head.
What shape is the pesäpallo infield?
The infield is pentagonal and about 96 metres long, with the bases in a zig-zag.
What is a pesäpallo hit that reaches the third base called?
Balls hit out of the field on the fly are fouls, so the third base is as far as it goes.
What is a pesäpallo substitute called who may bat at any point in the order?
Each side has nine batters and three jokers, who can be slotted in as needed.
What is the top league of Finnish pesäpallo called?
Below it come Ykköspesis, Suomensarja and the regional Maakuntasarja.
At which Olympic Games was pesäpallo shown as a demonstration sport?
Finland's own game was played for the crowds at the Helsinki Games.
Why did helmets become compulsory in pesäpallo?
A player was killed by a ball in 1985
A rule change at the 1992 World Cup
Jari Kettunen was struck on the head and died, and the rule followed.
Which annual pesäpallo all-star match divides Finland in two?
The Itä-Länsi match is played each year in June or early July.
How old was Matti Nykänen when he won his first world title, at Oslo in 1982?
Born in July 1963, he took the large hill world title as a teenager.
At which hill did Matti Nykänen win the ski flying world title in 1985?
He also took four overall World Cup titles, in 1983, 1985, 1986 and 1988.
What did Matti Nykänen take up after ski jumping, selling 25,000 copies of his first try?
His album Yllätysten yö came out in 1992 and went gold in Finland.
What rule did the International Ski Federation change after Mieto's defeat by 0.01 seconds?
Times were rounded to a tenth of a second
The federation decided to stop measuring cross-country races in hundredths.
How many Olympic medals did Juha Mieto win altogether?
One gold, two silver and two bronze across four Winter Games.
To which Finnish body was the skier Juha Mieto elected in 2007?
He was elected for the Centre Party in the Vaasa constituency with 13,768 votes.
How many goals did Teemu Selänne score in his record-breaking rookie NHL season?
His 76 goals in 1992-93 for Winnipeg is still the record for a rookie.
Which NHL team drafted Teemu Selänne tenth overall in 1988?
He stayed in Finland four more years before crossing to Winnipeg.
With which club did Teemu Selänne win the Stanley Cup in 2007?
It came in his sixteenth NHL season, at the age of 36.
What was Teemu Selänne's nickname in North America?
He scored 684 goals in the NHL and went into the Hall of Fame in 2017.
How old was Teemu Selänne when he played his last NHL game?
His final game was in May 2014, twenty-two years after his first.
With which team did Mika Häkkinen make his Formula One debut in 1991?
He debuted at the United States Grand Prix, qualified thirteenth and retired.
At which 1995 Grand Prix did a tyre failure nearly kill Mika Häkkinen?
He fractured his skull in qualifying at Adelaide and spent two months in hospital.
How many Grand Prix victories did Mika Häkkinen take in his career?
His first came at the European Grand Prix of 1997 and his last in the United States in 2001.
Which Icelandic volcano erupted in 1783 and 1784 and poisoned harvests across Europe?
The Laki fissure, part of the Grímsvötn system, is one of Iceland's most destructive eruptions.
Which Icelandic volcano shut down European air traffic in 2010?
Its ash cloud grounded flights across the continent for days.
Which is the highest of Iceland's volcanoes, at over 2,100 metres?
Öræfajökull reaches 2,119 m and last erupted in 1727.
An eruption in 1973 buried part of a town on Heimaey. Which volcano was it?
Eldfell rose on the island of Heimaey and its lava ran into the harbour.
Which Icelandic volcano gave the long eruption of 934, among the largest in the island's history?
Eldgjá is a great eruptive fissure of the Katla system.
Which ancient shield does Finland's bedrock belong to?
Its three domains, Kola, Karelian and Svecofennian, merged about 1,800 million years ago.
In which parts of Finland are the oldest, Archean rocks found?
The eastern and northern bedrock is mainly Archean granitoid and migmatitic gneiss.
Where in Finland is rapakivi granite, the crumbling stone, chiefly found?
Rapakivi intruded in the Mesoproterozoic and lies thickest in Åland and the south-east.
Roughly how much rock did the ice ages grind off Finland on average?
The figure is an average: glacial erosion varied enormously from place to place.
Which part of Finland became free of the ice sheet first?
The south-east cleared shortly before the Younger Dryas cold spell, 12,700 years ago.
By roughly how long ago had the ice sheet left almost all of Finland?
The lower Tornio valley in the north-west was the last ground to clear.
Where did mining in Finland begin, in 1530?
Mining stayed small until the 1930s, when Finnish industry took it up in earnest.
In which year was the Outokumpu ore deposit discovered?
It was Finland's first sulphide ore mine and ran until 1989.
Which metal was mined at Petsamo until Finland lost the area in 1944?
The Canadian company INCO worked the Petsamo nickel from the 1920s onwards.
What is the highest temperature ever measured in Finland?
It was recorded at Joensuu airport on 29 July 2010.
Where was Finland's highest temperature ever recorded?
The reading of 37.2 degrees came at Joensuu airport on 29 July 2010.
What is the lowest temperature ever measured in Finland?
It was measured at Pokka in Kittilä on 28 January 1999.
In which Lapland municipality was Finland's coldest temperature measured?
Pokka in Kittilä read minus 51.5 degrees in January 1999.
Which is the second oldest town in Finland, with rights from 1346?
Turku is older still; Porvoo got its charter in 1346 and Rauma in 1442.
In which year did Rauma become a town?
Rauma and Naantali, a year apart, are among the five oldest Finnish towns.
In which year was Oulu founded as a town?
Oulu came a year before Vaasa, in the Swedish push to found towns on the northern coast.
In which year did Tampere become a town?
Gustav III granted Tampere its charter; Lahti had to wait until 1905.
Since which year has there been no legal difference between a Finnish town and a municipality?
A Finnish municipality may simply call itself a city if it thinks it looks like one.
In which year did Kangasala take the title of city?
Kangasala is the most recent Finnish municipality to have taken the name.
Which six Finnish towns all took town rights in the same year, 1960?
